$comment: Public benchmark suites as data (c49). Adding a suite is a data addition: no code changes. argv/env templates use {base_url} {api_key} {model} {output_dir}; argv is a list, never a shell string. `scorer` is the upstream's OWN scorer; `scorer.result` says which file it writes and how a score is read from it. `verified: false` marks entry points taken from upstream docs but not run here.

suites.name: bfcl
suites.version: bfcl-eval (pin at first operator run; BFCL v3/v4 categories)
suites.install_hint: pip install bfcl-eval (not the unrelated `bfcl` package)
suites.verified_note: Command names and flags (--model, --test-category, --skip-server-setup, --result-dir, --score-dir, REMOTE_OPENAI_*) confirmed from the upstream README; the --model value for a custom endpoint and the data_overall.csv column name were not run.

suites.name: mmmu
suites.version: lmms-eval mmmu_val (pin at first operator run)
suites.verified_note: Chosen over the official MMMU repo because lmms-eval ships the mmmu_val task with an OpenAI-compatible client (--model openai, OPENAI_API_KEY; documented 'any OpenAI-compatible endpoint'); the exact base-URL variable (assumed OPENAI_API_BASE) and the results JSON key were not verified.

suites.name: livecodebench
suites.version: LiveCodeBench release_latest (pin release_version at first operator run)
suites.verified_note: lcb_runner.runner.main flags (--model, --scenario codegeneration, --evaluate, --release_version) confirmed from the README; its docs do not describe an OpenAI-compatible endpoint option (needs a model entry in lm_styles.py), and the eval-file layout/pass@1 key are unverified.
